target.name: Polar Semiconductor

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Growth → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.2x) to $700M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Chips & Semiconductors (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 12 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Polar Semiconductor is a Growth-stage semiconductor company that has raised $700M+ across equity and state programs. The comparable universe spans 3 public peers (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private companies in the Chips & Semiconductors sector, though the narrow peer set—companies at identical stage and valuation tier—remains constrained.

Stage-progression analysis provides the primary quantitative anchor. Starting from $700M in total capital raised as a valuation proxy, application of a standard 1.2x step-up multiplier for progression within the Growth stage yields $840M. This method is applicable given the company's disclosed funding history and clear stage positioning, though it relies on the assumption that raised capital reasonably proxies pre-money valuation absent disclosed revenue or comparable transaction data.

Peer-median and public-comp anchoring methods do not apply here. The Chips & Semiconductors sector contains only 12 same-sector peers, and filtering for identical stage and valuation tier yields insufficient datapoints (minimum three required). Public comparables show a 18.4x P/S median across ALAB, NVDA, and AMD, but Polar Semiconductor's revenue is not on file, precluding P/S multiple application. The triangulated range of $714M to $966M (median $840M) reflects methodological constraints. Key uncertainties include revenue run-rate, unit economics, and technology differentiation relative to the identified private peer set.
